For a random variable $Z \sim N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a > 0{:}$

$$
P(Z \gt -a) = P(Z \lt a) = \Phi(a)
$$

We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P( Z > -0.76).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/fbacbbe3f53c73316fd070d95e4c077cd695bdcf884d30a95f6b0850df328c80.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z \lt 0.76).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/c0f612336c02eee97d6c66b56f0854286b3a23b90053810e9e4fb75b698b5a60.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z > -0.76)
= P(Z < 0.76)
= \Phi(0.76)
= 0.7764.
$$

e-13271.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval Using the Complement
e-13271.worked_solution:

For a random variable $Z \sim N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a > 0{:}$

$$
P(Z \gt a) = P(Z \lt -a) = \Phi(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P( Z \lt -1.54).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/52d4c1add91819ff1f9dddf609b5753506c26e6cd6ee7f3cb14150ccb9b60971.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z \gt 1.54).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/7fef056bb5564986a009198685a2951de87ccb8e09c932c6902bfafdcdf0656f.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-1.54) & =P(Z>1.54) \\  & =1-P(Z<1.54) \\  & =1-Φ(1.54) \\  & =1-0.9382 \\  & =0.0618.\end{aligned}
$$

e-13269.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on a Bounded Interval
e-13269.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.53 <        Z <        0.53).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/bb86bde3595d6a64d1cd82da3c928f28c496f495f9c6815e56ee025a4a69d685.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$ 

$$
P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.53<Z<0.53) & =P(Z<0.53)-P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.53)-P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =Φ(0.53)-Φ(-0.53)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(0.53) = 0.7019,
$$

but we are not given $\Phi(-0.53) .$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.53) & =P(Z\le -0.53) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.53) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.53) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.53) \\  & =1-Φ(0.53) \\  & =1-0.7019 \\  & =0.2981\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.53<Z<0.53) & =Φ(0.53)-Φ(-0.53) \\  & =0.7019-0.2981 \\  & =0.4038.\end{aligned}
$$

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>2.31).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/a3e01ca4fd737cea9afe95374a17c0428f83a6717d98a7557222a856aa2d0c02.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>2.31)=P(Z<-2.31)=Φ(-2.31)=0.0104.
$$

For a random variable Z∼N(0,1) we have the following symmetry property for a>0:

P(Z>−a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<1.65).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<1.65) & =P(Z>-1.65) \\  & =1-P(Z<-1.65) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.65) \\  & =1-0.0495 \\  & =0.9505.\end{aligned}

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
